title: Yogācārabhūmi
alt_titles: Yuqie shidi lun 瑜伽師地論 (T1579)

attribution.tradition: Chinese tradition: spoken by Maitreya (Xuanzang's translation names Maitreya); Tibetan tradition: composed by Asaṅga
attribution.scholarly: a compilation of several layers by the early Yogācāra community, the Śrāvakabhūmi among the oldest

structure.description: Basic section of seventeen stages (bhūmi): 1 the five sense-consciousnesses, 2 mind, 3 with initial and sustained thought, 4 without initial but with sustained thought, 5 without either, 6 concentrated, 7 unconcentrated, 8 with mind, 9 without mind, 10 made of hearing, 11 made of reflection, 12 made of cultivation, 13 śrāvakas, 14 pratyekabuddhas, 15 bodhisattvas, 16 with remainder, 17 without remainder; followed by four compendia (Viniścaya-, Vastu-, Paryāya-, Vivaraṇa-saṃgrahaṇī)

summary: The encyclopaedic foundation of Yogācāra: an analysis of consciousness, the grounds of meditation and the paths of the three vehicles, in which the store-consciousness (ālaya-vijñāna) is first argued for (in the Viniścayasaṃgrahaṇī) and the bodhisattva's training, discipline and grounds are laid out.

editions.name: V. Bhattacharya, The Yogācārabhūmi of Ācārya Asaṅga, Part I (bhūmis 1–5), Calcutta 1957 — local e-text (asian_classics_hk)
editions.licence: ancient text public domain; e-text for research use (DSBC / GRETIL terms)

notes: Sanskrit survives for large parts (Śrāvakabhūmi, Bodhisattvabhūmi, bhūmis 1–5 and others); the complete text is extant in Chinese (100 fascicles) and Tibetan. Taishō numbers are recalled, not checked locally (CBETA T30–31 not in sources_raw).

title: Śrāvakabhūmi

attribution.scholarly: probably the oldest layer of the Yogācārabhūmi

structure.description: Four yogasthānas preceded by the gotra-, avatāra- and naiṣkramya-bhūmis (Shukla ed.)

summary: A meditation manual for the disciples' path: the lineage and entry into the teaching, renunciation, the prerequisites of morality and sense-restraint, the four kinds of meditation object (pervasive, purifying temperament, skill, purifying defilement), the nine stages of settling the mind with six powers and four attentions, the seven attentions leading to the absorptions, and the mundane and supramundane paths.

title: Bodhisattvabhūmi
alt_titles: Pusa di chi jing 菩薩地持經 (T1581, Dharmakṣema)

scholarly.text: c. 4th c. CE; translated by Dharmakṣema in the early 5th c.

structure.description: Three yogasthānas: ādhāra (18 paṭalas: gotra, cittotpāda, svaparārtha, tattvārtha, prabhāva, paripāka, bodhi, balagotra, dāna, śīla, kṣānti, vīrya, dhyāna, prajñā, saṃgrahavastu, pūjā-sevā-apramāṇa, bodhipakṣya, bodhisattvaguṇa), ādhārānudharma (4: liṅga, pakṣa, adhyāśaya, vihāra), ādhāraniṣṭha (6: upapatti, parigraha, bhūmi, caryā, lakṣaṇānuvyañjana, pratiṣṭhā)

summary: The bodhisattva's path in full: the lineage (gotra) of bodhisattvas, the arising of the resolve for awakening, the meaning of reality as the inexpressible object of non-conceptual cognition, the perfections — with the chapter on discipline (śīla-paṭala) that became the source of the bodhisattva vows in Tibet and East Asia — the abodes and grounds, and the qualities of a buddha.

editions.name: U. Wogihara 1930–36; N. Dutt 1966 — local GRETIL Devanāgarī e-text
editions.licence: ancient text public domain; e-text for research use (DSBC / GRETIL terms)

title: Viniścayasaṃgrahaṇī
alt_titles: rnam par gtan la dbab pa bsdu ba
summary: The Yogācārabhūmi's compendium of ascertainments, which opens with the proofs (by eight reasons) that a store-consciousness must exist and discusses its relation to the afflicted mind and the seeds; also the three natures and the transformation of the basis.
notes: The eight proofs of the ālaya are recalled as being at the opening of the Viniścayasaṃgrahaṇī; Sanskrit survives only in fragments.

title: Vastusaṃgrahaṇī
summary: The compendium of topics, commenting on the sūtra and vinaya material of the Saṃyuktāgama and the monastic code (mātṛkā) within the Yogācārabhūmi.

title: Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra
alt_titles: theg pa chen po mdo sde'i rgyan
Dasheng zhuangyan jing lun 大乘莊嚴經論 (T1604)

attribution.tradition: Tibetan: verses by Maitreya, received by Asaṅga, prose by Vasubandhu; Chinese (T1604): attributed to Asaṅga
attribution.scholarly: verses and commentary from the Asaṅga–Vasubandhu circle, authorship of verses vs. bhāṣya debated

structure.description: 21 chapters (adhikāra) in Lévi's edition, incl. ch. 3 gotra, ch. 4 cittotpāda, ch. 6 tattva, ch. 9 bodhi (three bodies, four wisdoms), ch. 11 dharmaparyeṣṭi, ch. 14 avavādānuśāsanī (the meditative entry into mind-only), ch. 16 pāramitā

summary: A verse summa of the bodhisattva path in the light of Yogācāra: why the Mahāyāna is the Buddha's word, the lineages, the arising of the mind of awakening, reality as neither existent nor non-existent, awakening with its three bodies and four wisdoms, and the meditative stages by which the bodhisattva sees objects as mental speech, rests in mind-only and then abandons even that to reach the first ground.

editions.name: S. Lévi, Paris 1907 — local GRETIL e-text (J. Braarvig)
editions.licence: ancient text public domain; e-text for research use (DSBC / GRETIL terms)

notes: One of the 'five Dharmas of Maitreya' in the Tibetan list (Abhisamayālaṃkāra, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra, Madhyāntavibhāga, Dharmadharmatāvibhāga, Ratnagotravibhāga). Chinese tradition instead attributes the Yogācārabhūmi to Maitreya and the Ratnagotravibhāga to Sāramati.

alt_titles: mdo sde'i rgyan gyi bshad pa

title: Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāraṭīkā
summary: Asvabhāva's commentary on the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra, extant in Tibetan.

title: Madhyāntavibhāga
alt_titles: Distinguishing the Middle from the Extremes
dbus dang mtha' rnam par 'byed pa
Bian zhongbian lun 辯中邊論 (T1600, Xuanzang; verses T1601)

attribution.tradition: verses by Maitreya received by Asaṅga; commentary by Vasubandhu

structure.description: 5 chapters: 1 characteristics (lakṣaṇa: unreal imagination, the three natures, emptiness), 2 obscurations (āvaraṇa), 3 reality (tattva), 4 cultivation of the antidotes, stages and fruits, 5 the supremacy of the vehicle

summary: The Maitreya text that defines the Yogācāra middle way: unreal imagination exists, the duality of grasped and grasper within it does not, and emptiness exists within it; hence everything is neither empty nor non-empty. It analyses the obscurations, ten kinds of reality, the path with its five faults of meditation and eight remedies, and the ten perfections.

title: Madhyāntavibhāgabhāṣya
alt_titles: dbus dang mtha' rnam par 'byed pa'i 'grel pa
summary: Vasubandhu's commentary on the Madhyāntavibhāga verses, which glosses unreal imagination as the imagination of grasped and grasper and emptiness as its being devoid of that duality.

title: Madhyāntavibhāgaṭīkā
alt_titles: dbus dang mtha' rnam par 'byed pa'i 'grel bshad
summary: Sthiramati's sub-commentary on Vasubandhu's Madhyāntavibhāgabhāṣya, recovered in Sanskrit (Nepalese manuscript) in the twentieth century.

title: Dharmadharmatāvibhāga
alt_titles: chos dang chos nyid rnam par 'byed pa

tradition.text: taught by Maitreya to Asaṅga; the tradition says it was hidden and rediscovered by Maitrīpa

scholarly.text: c. 4th c. CE text; transmitted to Tibet in the 11th c.

structure.description: Prose and verse versions (Derge D4022 prose, D4023 verse)

summary: A short Maitreya text distinguishing dharmas — the appearance of duality and of names, which is saṃsāra — from their nature (dharmatā) — suchness without the division of grasped and grasper, which is nirvāṇa — and teaching the entry into non-conceptual wisdom and the transformation of the basis in ten aspects.
notes: One of the 'five Dharmas of Maitreya' in the Tibetan list (Abhisamayālaṃkāra, Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra, Madhyāntavibhāga, Dharmadharmatāvibhāga, Ratnagotravibhāga). Chinese tradition instead attributes the Yogācārabhūmi to Maitreya and the Ratnagotravibhāga to Sāramati. The account of Maitrīpa's rediscovery (with the Ratnagotravibhāga) is the Tibetan tradition's; not in Chinese.

title: Dharmadharmatāvibhāgavṛtti
summary: Vasubandhu's commentary on the Dharmadharmatāvibhāga, extant in Tibetan.

title: Abhisamayālaṃkāra

attribution.tradition: taught by Maitreya (Tibetan list of five Maitreya texts)
attribution.scholarly: author unknown; not known in China; earliest commentary by Ārya Vimuktisena

structure.description: 8 chapters (the eight topics: three knowledges — all-aspect knowledge, knowledge of paths, knowledge of bases; four trainings — full realization of all aspects, the peak, the serial, the instantaneous; the dharmakāya), treated through 70 points

summary: A verse outline of the hidden meaning of the Prajñāpāramitā sūtras as a path: eight topics and seventy points laying out the arising of the mind of awakening, the five paths, the ten grounds and the bodies of a buddha. It became the backbone of the Tibetan monastic curriculum on the perfection of wisdom.

title: Mahāyānasaṃgraha
alt_titles: theg pa chen po bsdus pa
She dasheng lun 攝大乘論 (T1593 Paramārtha; T1594 Xuanzang; T1592 Buddhaśānta)

structure.description: 10 chapters on ten distinctive features of the Mahāyāna: 1 the basis of knowables (ālaya-vijñāna), 2 the characteristics of knowables (three natures), 3 entry into them (vijñaptimātratā), 4 the causes and fruits of entry (perfections), 5 cultivation (ten grounds), 6 higher discipline, 7 higher mind, 8 higher wisdom (non-conceptual cognition), 9 the fruit as abandonment (non-abiding nirvāṇa, transformation of the basis), 10 the fruit as wisdom (three bodies)

summary: Asaṅga's systematic summa of Yogācāra, proving the store-consciousness, defining the three natures, describing the entry into cognition-only, and presenting the path, the three trainings, non-conceptual wisdom, non-abiding nirvāṇa and the three bodies as the ten points in which the Mahāyāna surpasses other vehicles.

title: Triṃśikā (Triṃśikāvijñaptikārikā)
alt_titles: Weishi sanshi lun song 唯識三十論頌 (T1586, Xuanzang)

structure.description: 30 verses: 1–16 the threefold transformation of consciousness (store, mind, object-apprehension, with the mental factors); 17–19 cognition-only and the cause of rebirth; 20–25 the three natures and three naturelessnesses; 26–30 the path to the transformation of the basis

summary: Vasubandhu's compact statement of the whole Yogācāra system: all talk of self and dharmas refers to the transformation of consciousness in three forms, so everything is cognition-only; the three natures and naturelessnesses; and the path on which, when cognition no longer apprehends an object, the yogin abides in cognition-only and attains the supramundane, non-apprehending wisdom and the transformation of the basis.
